result.rationale: Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), so raw_html=1 and regular=0. The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` sets all existing posts to 1 (raw_html), and Post#cook in this diff returns `raw` when cook_method == raw_html, so historical markdown posts would render uncooked. The default should be 0.

judged_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 sets every existing post to cook_method=1, which per Post.cook_methods Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) is :raw_html. After this migration runs, every pre-existing post in the database is silently reclassified as raw HTML: Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:131-134) returns raw uncooked text for cook_method == :raw_html, so all historical markdown posts render their raw markdown source to users. The default should be 0 (:regular); the migration backfills the entire table with the wrong value and there is no correcting backfill step.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the claim that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` maps `:regular` to 0 and `:raw_html` to 1, making the migration default (`default: 1`) equal to `:raw_html`. The diff does not support that mapping. In fact, existing code uses the same `Enum` pattern for `Post.types` (`Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`), and in Discourse this convention is typically 1-based (e.g., regular posts commonly have `post_type = 1`). Under that (implied) convention, `default: 1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so the described mass reclassification/markdown breakage is not verifiable from the diff.
